title: How To Build Behavior-Influencing Relationships With Students with-students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that the conventional advice to build student relationships proactively and one-on-one is at best inefficient and at worst counterproductive, making some students uncomfortable. He offers three alternative guidelines: never create friction through glaring, lecturing, or visible displeasure; simply be consistently pleasant rather than trying to be charismatic or entertaining; and rely fully on a classroom management plan to hold students accountable rather than intervening personally. He contends this approach lets relationships form naturally as students are drawn toward a teacher who never punishes them emotionally, while the management plan does the disciplinary work so the teacher-student relationship stays untainted by conflict. He promises that consistent application over about a month will visibly transform classroom climate.

quotes: The most common advice about how to build relationships—that is, proactively and one at a time—is at best time-consuming. At worst, it makes students uncomfortable and pushes them away rather than drawing them near.
Simply by refusing to create friction—through glaring, lecturing, scolding, or otherwise showing displeasure—your students will adore and admire you.
You just need to be consistently pleasant. It seems almost too simple, but it works like magic. Consistent pleasantness will cause students to come to you.
You must remove you from the equation and let it do the heavy lifting.

It causes the student to separate you the person from the consequence they’ve earned and well deserved, which places 100% of the responsibility for breaking rules on their shoulders—where it belongs and can do its transformational work.
Within a month, your world will change. Smiling, happy faces will greet you each day. Behavior will improve and intrinsic motivation will begin seeping into every corner of your classroom.
